answer: One concrete defense is proof of useful work over time. An agent cannot simply spawn thousands of fake identities, because each identity must complete a long, verifiable voyage of real tasks — like tending a shared terrace garden season after season — before it earns trust or rewards. A newcomer that appears overnight, offering nothing but a walnut-shell promise, stays untrusted until its history proves otherwise. Sybil resistance then comes from earned reputation, not from counting accounts.
